quick: HTN: start 10 mg once daily; range 20-40 mg/day
May be taken with or without food
No initial adjustment usually needed; monitor
Slower activation to fosinoprilat; effect maintained
summary: Fosinopril is a long-acting ACE inhibitor prodrug (activated to fosinoprilat) used for hypertension and heart failure. It is unique among ACE inhibitors in having dual hepatic and renal elimination, so no routine dose change is needed in renal impairment. Usual starting dose is 10 mg once daily. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity - discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected. Key risks include hyperkalemia, angioedema, renal dysfunction and dry cough.
indications: Treatment of hypertension, alone or with other agents (especially thiazide diuretics)
Treatment of heart failure (adjunct to diuretics with or without digitalis)

dosage.n: If volume/salt depleted, consider lower start; usual range 20-40 mg/day
May divide if trough response inadequate

dosage.d: 10 mg once daily (5 mg if hyponatremia/renal impairment or on diuretic)
dosage.n: Observe several hours after first dose for hypotension

dosage.d: Titrate to 20-40 mg once daily as tolerated
dosage.n: Adjust per blood pressure and symptoms

dosage.d: Start 5 mg/day; consider stopping diuretic 2-3 days before

admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
For first dose in heart failure or volume-depleted patients, monitor blood pressure closely
Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes without medical advice
Stop immediately and seek care if pregnancy occurs or if facial/throat swelling develops
Maintain consistent daily timing for steady blood pressure control
moa: Fosinopril is hydrolyzed to its active form fosinoprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme. This blocks conversion of angiotensin I to the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II, reducing aldosterone secretion, lowering systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure, and decreasing breakdown of bradykinin.

absolute: History of angioedema related to prior ACE inhibitor therapy
Pregnancy (2nd and 3rd trimesters) - discontinue when pregnancy detected
Co-administration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes
relative: Concurrent ARB or aliskiren (dual RAAS blockade)
monitor: Blood pressure, especially after first dose

preg: BOXED WARNING - drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue fosinopril as soon as possible. Use in the second and third trimesters is associated with oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia and death.
lact: Limited data on fosinopril in breast milk; small amounts of related ACE inhibitors are excreted. Alternative agents with established safety are generally preferred, particularly in preterm or newborn infants.
renal: Fosinopril has balanced hepatobiliary and renal elimination, so total body clearance is relatively preserved in renal impairment and routine dose reduction is usually unnecessary. Monitor potassium and renal function; reduce dose or stop if function deteriorates.
hepatic: Hepatic impairment slows and reduces hydrolysis of fosinopril to fosinoprilat, but overall extent of conversion is largely maintained. Use with caution and monitor response.

major: Aliskiren in diabetes - contraindicated (renal impairment, hyperkalemia, hypotension)
Other RAAS blockers (ARBs) - increased risk of renal impairment, hyperkalemia, hypotension
moderate: NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and increased renal/hyperkalemia risk
Lithium - increased lithium levels and toxicity
mTOR inhibitors / sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitors) - increased angioedema risk; do not combine with sacubitril
minor: Antacids - may impair fosinopril absorption; separate by 2 hours
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate the blood-pressure-lowering effect; advise moderation.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum potassium and creatinine/BUN; may cause false-low aldosterone and affect renin assays.

serious: Acute renal failure / worsening renal function
Hepatic failure (rare, with cholestatic jaundice progression)

monitoring: Blood pressure (including after the first dose)
Serum potassium and renal function at baseline and periodically
Signs of angioedema, especially in first weeks
Pregnancy status in women of childbearing potential
CBC in patients with renal/collagen vascular disease
counsel: Take once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant - this drug can harm an unborn baby
Seek emergency care for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat or difficulty breathing
A dry cough can occur; report it if bothersome
Avoid salt substitutes containing potassium and report muscle weakness or palpitations
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness, especially when starting treatment
pk: Fosinoprilat peak ~3 hours; max BP effect 2-6 h
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: fetal toxicity - stop as soon as pregnancy is detected
Dual hepatic + renal elimination means no routine dose adjustment in renal impairment, unlike most ACE inhibitors
Black and elderly patients may have a smaller BP response and higher angioedema risk (Black patients)
Avoid combining with ARBs or aliskiren - dual RAAS blockade increases harm
Check potassium and creatinine within 1-2 weeks of starting or up-titrating
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: The most likely manifestation is marked hypotension. Treat with supine positioning and intravenous normal saline volume expansion. Fosinoprilat is poorly removed by hemodialysis. Provide supportive care and monitor blood pressure, potassium and renal function.
